stories.title: Hodler's Digest: 'white hats' recover 4,000 BTC from Liquid as ETFs post 2026's best inflows
stories.summary: Cointelegraph's weekly Hodler's Digest reports that so-called 'white hat' actors recovered 4,000 BTC tied to the Liquid exchange, in the same week that Bitcoin ETFs logged their strongest inflows of 2026. As a roundup, the digest bundles both items together without breaking out full details on either.
stories.whyItMatters: A large fund recovery and record ETF demand both speak to how the market is handling security risk and institutional appetite right now.
whatToWatch: Follow-up reporting naming who carried out the Liquid recovery
Whether the ETF inflow pace mentioned holds into the next week
questions: Who conducted the 'white hat' recovery, and how?
Which ETFs specifically drove the 2026 high inflow week?

sources.title: ‘White hats’ take 4000 BTC from Liquid, ETFs see best inflows of 2026: Hodler’s Digest

stories.title: Harmony proposes shutting down its layer-1 chain, migrating ONE to Ethereum
stories.summary: Harmony has put forward a proposal to shut down its own layer-1 blockchain and move its native ONE token to Ethereum, according to Cointelegraph. The report did not detail a timeline or the governance process for the proposal.
stories.whyItMatters: A once-independent layer-1 giving up its own chain in favor of Ethereum points to continued consolidation among smaller networks.
whatToWatch: Harmony community or governance vote on the proposal
Any published migration timeline if the plan advances
questions: Will ONE holders need to swap tokens, and on what terms?
What happens to existing apps built on Harmony's chain?

stories.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows drop 76% heading into Labor Day as only BlackRock and Fidelity gain
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETF inflows fell 76% entering the Labor Day break, CryptoSlate reports, with only funds from BlackRock and Fidelity attracting fresh money. Other issuers saw flows stall or reverse over the period.
stories.whyItMatters: Demand narrowing to just two issuers raises the question of whether institutional interest in Bitcoin ETFs is broadening or concentrating.
whatToWatch: Flow data once trading normalizes after the holiday
Whether smaller issuers regain net inflows
questions: Is the drop seasonal, or an early sign of cooling demand?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows fall 76% entering Labor Day break as only BlackRock and Fidelity attract fresh money

stories.title: Dormant Satoshi-era wallet moves 600 BTC after 16 years
stories.summary: A Bitcoin wallet dating back roughly 16 years, to the Satoshi era, became active and moved 600 BTC, Cointelegraph reports. The report does not say who controls the wallet or where the coins were sent.
stories.whyItMatters: Movements from long-dormant early wallets draw scrutiny because they can signal early holders cashing out, though the cause here is unconfirmed.
whatToWatch: Whether the coins move again toward an exchange
On-chain analysts attempting to identify the wallet's owner
questions: Who controls the wallet, and why move now?
Is this a sale, an internal transfer, or a security precaution?

sources.title: Satoshi-era Bitcoin wakes after 16 years of dormancy as 600 BTC moves

stories.title: The $63 billion revolving door behind the entire US Bitcoin ETF market
stories.summary: CryptoSlate examines how an estimated $63 billion cycles through a small group of authorized participants and market makers that underpin the entire US spot Bitcoin ETF market. The piece frames ETF liquidity as concentrated among relatively few firms rather than broadly distributed.
stories.whyItMatters: How concentrated ETF liquidity is affects how resilient that market would be if a major participant pulled back.
whatToWatch: Any disclosures on which firms dominate ETF creation and redemption activity
questions: How much systemic risk does this concentration create?

sources.title: The $63 billion revolving door carrying the entire US Bitcoin ETF market

stories.title: How Bitmine could pass its 5% Ethereum supply goal without further buying
stories.summary: CryptoSlate outlines how Bitmine could exceed its stated goal of holding 5% of Ethereum's total supply without making additional purchases, pointing to factors beyond direct buying. The piece does not specify further mechanics beyond that framing.
stories.whyItMatters: Large corporate ETH holdings shrink circulating supply and shape how the market reads institutional accumulation of Ethereum.
whatToWatch: Bitmine's disclosed ETH holdings in upcoming reports
questions: What specific mechanism would push Bitmine past 5% without new buying?

stories.title: Three DeFi projects risk exclusion from future Arbitrum DAO programs
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that three DeFi projects built on Arbitrum face possible exclusion from future Arbitrum DAO incentive programs. The projects and the DAO's specific reasoning were not named in the report.
stories.whyItMatters: DAO incentive decisions determine which protocols receive funded liquidity and growth support on Arbitrum.
whatToWatch: A DAO vote or announcement naming the affected projects
The DAO's stated rationale for possible exclusion
questions: Which projects are at risk, and what triggered the review?

stories.title: Tether-backed exchange Orionx to shut down after audit finds $7M custody gap
stories.summary: Orionx, an exchange backed by Tether, will shut down after an audit uncovered a $7 million gap in customer custody, according to Cointelegraph. The report does not detail the cause of the shortfall or Tether's role beyond its backing.
stories.whyItMatters: A custody failure at an exchange tied to the largest stablecoin issuer raises fresh questions about counterparty risk across crypto.
whatToWatch: Details on whether affected customers recover their funds
Any statement from Tether on its exposure or response
questions: Will customers be made whole, and by whom?

sources.title: Tether-backed Orionx to shut down after audit flags $7M custody gap

stories.title: Bitcoin faces a new macro backdrop as the Fed pulls back and Treasury ramps up issuance
stories.summary: CryptoSlate describes a shifting macro environment for Bitcoin, in which the Federal Reserve is pulling back liquidity support even as the US Treasury increases debt issuance. The piece frames this combination as an unusual setup for crypto markets going forward.
stories.whyItMatters: Macro liquidity conditions have driven past crypto cycles, so a shift in Fed and Treasury behavior matters beyond crypto-specific news.
whatToWatch: Upcoming Fed policy signals
Treasury issuance schedules and their effect on market liquidity
questions: How exactly would this liquidity mix affect Bitcoin demand?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s faces a weird new macro reality as the Fed turns off the tap and Treasury opens the floodgates

stories.title: Solana ETF inflows fall 97% for the week as CME funds trim their net-short position
stories.summary: Weekly inflows into Solana ETFs dropped 97%, while CME-based Solana funds became less net-short over the same period, CryptoSlate reports.
stories.whyItMatters: A near-total inflow slowdown alongside easing short positioning gives a mixed signal on institutional sentiment toward Solana.
whatToWatch: Next week's Solana ETF flow figures
Whether CME positioning turns net long
questions: What drove the sharp drop in inflows this week?

sources.title: Solana’s weekly ETF inflows fell 97% while CME funds became less net short

stories.title: Inside the 15-minute trading pulse moving $14 billion in Bitcoin perpetual futures
stories.summary: CryptoSlate examines a recurring 15-minute trading pattern it says moves roughly $14 billion in Bitcoin perpetual futures volume. The report focuses on market structure rather than a single news event.
stories.whyItMatters: Recurring patterns in derivatives markets help explain short-term Bitcoin volatility that has nothing to do with news.
whatToWatch: Whether the pattern persists or gets arbitraged away over time
questions: What is driving the 15-minute cadence — bots, rebalancing, or something else?

stories.title: Stablecoins won't scale without banks, Decrypt argues
stories.summary: A Decrypt piece argues that stablecoins cannot reach greater scale without deeper involvement from traditional banks. It frames bank participation, rather than crypto-native infrastructure alone, as the bottleneck for further stablecoin growth.
stories.whyItMatters: Stablecoins underpin most crypto trading and payments, so their path to scale affects the market's broader infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Any bank moves into stablecoin issuance, custody, or settlement partnerships
questions: Which specific bank functions are needed — custody, settlement, or something else?
